terms.gloss: an echo, the image of a voice
evidence: Verg. G. 4.50: vōcisque offēnsa resultat imāgō
Hor. C. 1.12.3–4: cujus recinet jocōsa nōmen imāgō
terms.comment: The Latin word for an echo, the “image” of a voice (Lewis & Short: the pure Latin word); ēchō is the Greek one, and as a proper name the nymph.

phrases.latin: Clāmā magnā vōce: imāgō vōcem tibi reddet.
phrases.english: Shout loudly: the echo will give your voice back to you.

phrases.latin: aut ubi concava pulsū saxa sonant vōcisque offēnsa resultat imāgō
phrases.english: or where hollow rocks ring when struck, and the echo of a voice bounces back off them

phrases.latin: ut paternī flūminis rīpae simul et jocōsa redderet laudēs tibi Vāticānī montis imāgō
phrases.english: so that the banks of your native river and the playful echo of the Vatican hill gave back your praises together

sources: Lewis & Short: Echo · Lewis & Short: imago
